author: Mark Atwood
text:
CORRECTION 2026-11-24, before the fix. The description calls ConnectInfo on
the plain listener "deterministic". That was what I observed, twice, but the
cause was wrong: both reproductions were on /data with 0 bytes free and a
486 GB target/, and the I/O under teardown widened the window. After a
cargo clean I restored into_make_service_with_connect_info on the plain
listener and could not reproduce it at all: jmap_seed passes, and so does a
purpose-built attempt (one request, a pooled connection still open across
the stop). Treat the race as real but narrow, not deterministic.

FIXED by (b). mimid-agent-core gains StateLock::release, which unlocks
through a shared reference (File::unlock takes &self, so it works through
the Arc that Agent::state_lock hands out) and leaves the file in place;
unlocking twice and dropping afterwards are both harmless, and each lock is
on its own open file description, so a release never disturbs a newcomer's
lock. Daemon::serve calls store.state_lock().release() after every loop is
joined and both servers have returned, so "serve has returned" now means
the state directory is free whatever axum's drop order turns out to be.
ConnectInfo is back on the plain listener, which recovers the §7.1
per-source slowdown there (loopback gets LOOPBACK_FAILURES = 20) and ends
the divergence between the two listeners that the workaround had introduced.

The caller's promise, documented on release: it has stopped, so no clone
can begin work on the database again. A straggling clone is one being torn
down, not one that will write.

NO FAILING TEST, against AGENTS.md's "a bug fix starts with a regression
test, and that test must fail before the fix". There is nothing to make
fail: the race does not lose on a healthy machine, and the pre-fix
behaviour (lock held until the last Arc clone drops) is correct behaviour
for the old API. The evidence is the mechanism in axum 0.8.9's source,
quoted in the description. Two tests guard the contract from here on:
lock.rs's releasing_frees_the_lock_while_a_clone_is_still_alive (a unit
test of the new API) and jmap_network.rs's
the_state_directory_can_be_reopened_as_soon_as_serve_returns (the contract,
with a pooled connection open across the stop). Both say in their comments
that they are contract tests, not regression tests.
